decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<div dir="ltr" style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, as built PV system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting drawings and installation certificates by a MCS registered contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate at least the consented standards have been met:<br><br>a) Solar PV panels annual electricity peak generation of&nbsp;3.13&nbsp;kWp</div><div dir="ltr" style=""><br></div><div dir="ltr" style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net zero development and construction, in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan</div>

<p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</p><p>REASON: To protect acceptable local noise levels</p>

<div>A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the site against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the extension is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with current best practices.</div><div><br></div><div>REASON: In the interest of flood risk mitigation.</div>

<p>All new external facing and roofing materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works carried out in this connection) shall match those of the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance including type, size, colour, bond, pointing, coursing, jointing, profile and texture.</p><p>

REASON: In the interest of the visual amenity of the Victoria Park Conservation Area.</p>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="">Detailed drawings/full particulars of the proposed development showing the matters set out below must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, in writing, before work on the relevant part of the development commences. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved.</span></p><ul><li><span data-sheets-root="1" style="">Typical window and door details including sections at 1:20;</span></li></ul><p>REASON: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance.</p>

<p dir="ltr" style="line-height: 1.2; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 8pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The use hereby permitted, or the operation of any building services plant, shall not commence until a post-installation noise assessment has been carried out to confirm compliance with the noise criteria (Condition 10). The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and attenuation measures, and they shall be permanently retained and maintained in working order for the duration of the use and their operation.</span></p><p><br style=""></p><p dir="ltr" style="line-height: 1.2; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 8pt;"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Reason:</span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">&nbsp;To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area.</span></p><div><span style="font-size: 11pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><br></span></div>

<p>The use hereby permitted, or the operation of any building services plant, shall not commence until a post-installation noise assessment has been carried out to confirm compliance with the noise criteria (Condition 10). The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and attenuation measures, and they shall be permanently retained and maintained in working order for the duration of the use and their operation.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area.</p>

<div>Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp; maintenance plan (where applicable) of the living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat) and soakaway shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume.</div><div><br></div><div>REASON:&nbsp;In the interest of sustainable urban drainage.</div>

<div dir="ltr" style="">Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, full details including as built ASHP system (or any other related fixed plant adopted) specification and supporting drawings and installation certificates by a MCS registered contractor must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority<br>a) Minimum Heat pump Coefficient of Performance<br>b) Minimum Heat pump Seasonal Coefficient of Performance<br>c) Details of location of the condenser units from the heat pump systems and any noise solutions to mitigate the impact for nearby sensitive receptors<br></div><div dir="ltr" style=""><br></div><div dir="ltr" style="">REASON: In the interest of addressing climate change and securing sustainable and net zero development and construction, in accordance with LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan</div>

<p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, details and full specifications of 1 bird boxes, 1 swift bricks/boxes, and 1 bat boxes, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and shall be maintained for the lifespan of the development. The details should include:</p><p>A minimum of 1 swift bricks (same requirements for swift box) incorporated into the design of the development. They should be installed in groups of at least 2, and placed at or close to eaves level of the development hereby approved. They should be placed at least 5m above the ground with a 5m unobstructed flight path, both below and in front of the swift brick. The swift brick should be located facing north, east, or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided) and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Where possible, swift bricks should be set flush into the external wall to match adjacent brickwork.</p><p>A minimum of 1 bird boxes incorporated into the design of the development, with a variety of box types (including different sized entrance holes) to provide habitat for diverse bird species. The boxes should be installed at or close to the eaves level of the development hereby approved. The boxes should be between 3 and 5 metres from the ground, and there should be a clear flight path without any obstructions below and directly in front of the box. The boxes should be facing north, east or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided), and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Boxes located in the same area should not be placed too close together.&nbsp;</p><p>A minimum of 1 bat boxes incorporated into the design of the development. Boxes should be placed at or close to the eaves level of the development and at least 4m above the ground. The boxes should be placed away from artificial light sources and ideally located near dark tree lines or hedgerows where possible. The boxes should be located facing south, southeast or southwest, and exposed to sun for part of the day.</p><p>REASON: To support bird and bat populations, including swifts, in Hackney and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing nesting opportunities, in accordance with Hackney’s Local Plan LP33 policy LP47 which states that all development schemes involving buildings with an eaves height or roof commencement height of 5 metres and above are required to provide nesting boxes for swifts, sparrows, starlings, and/or bats as appropriate.</p>

<p style="">The air source heat pump hereby approved shall be mounted on suitable vibration isolation measures, including resilient vibration isolators positioned between the unit and any supporting brackets fixed to the external façade of the building. The vibration isolation measures shall be installed prior to first use of the air source heat pump and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.</p><p style="">REASON:&nbsp;To prevent the transmission of vibration and structure-borne noise to the building and neighbouring properties, in the interests of residential amenity.</p>

<p><span data-sheets-root="1" style="">No development shall commence until full details of the proposed Construction Methodology, in the form of a Construction Statement, is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Statement shall include details of the following relevant measures:<br><br>An introduction consisting of construction phase environmental management plan, definitions and abbreviations and project description and location;<br>A description of management responsibilities;<br>Measures to prevent the deposit of mud and debris on the public highway,<br>A description of the construction programme which identifies activities likely to cause high levels of noise or dust;<br>Site working hours and a named person for residents to contact;<br>Detailed Site logistics arrangements;<br>Details regarding parking, deliveries, and storage;<br>Details regarding dust and noise mitigation measures to be deployed including identification of sensitive receptors and ongoing monitoring;<br>A suitably qualified person shall develop a separate scheme of noise monitoring and management which shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.<br>Details of the hours of works and other measures to mitigate the impact of construction on the amenity of the area and safety of the highway network; and<br>Communication procedures with the Hackney Council and local community regarding key construction issues – newsletters, fliers etc.<br><br>The construction shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the details and measures approved in the Construction Statement for the related phase unless the written consent of the Local Planning Authority is received for any variation.<br><br>REASON: Development must not commence before this condition is discharged to avoid hazard and obstruction being caused to users of the public highway and to ensure minimal nuisance or disturbance is caused to the detriment of the amenities of adjoining occupiers and of the area generally and to avoid hazard and obstruction to the public highway.</span></p>
description: Ground Floor rear extension with green roof, First floor rear extension with flat roof, juliet balcony and internal amendments
